messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Paged KV cache error rate and eviction churn spike in us-west-2; auto-escalation to sev-2. Observed sustained metadata ops + heavy block eviction. Affected: hosted inference pools (redwood-hosted-prod).

maria: noticed higher 5xx on gen routes ~20m ago, got paged. seeing KV eviction rate 8x baseline, metadata RPCs spiking. tracing shows repeated blockmanager.handles.open -> evict cycles.

sam: copying logs: ``ERROR blockmgr: eviction failed reclaiming block 0x7f..: metadata leak detected, refcount mismatch`` repeated.

jordan: customers with heavy context (long chat sessions) reporting timeouts, one tenant (acme-inc) opened CS ticket for degraded latency. CS flagged as potential SLA breach. @customer-success FYI.

customer-success: logged ticket INC-4319, priority P1 for acme-inc. asking for ETA for mitigation and a short blurb I can send.

maria: initial triage: looks like recent rolling change to continuous-batch threshold and blocksize heuristics (deploy hash cf3a2 from 4h ago) changed batch grouping behavior for long sequences — causing uneven block hotness and aggressive eviction.

nate: I can revert the batch-threshold tweak quickly. We should consider a targeted rollback to pre-cf3a2 config for the affected pool.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline: rollback candidate detected for commit cf3a1 (previous). Manual approval required.

sam: mitigation plan: 1) throttle replacement eviction rate by bumping eviction.window_ms to 1000 temporarily 2) revert continuous_batch_threshold to 0.65 -> 0.5 (previous) 3) apply per-tenant rate-limits for the top 5 noisy tenants 4) canary the change to 2 instances then scale if stable. Need owners to run.

jordan: agree. also add a short-term defensive guard: drop max in-flight KV metadata requests to 30 to prevent further RPC storm.

maria: config diff I propose (applies to pool redwood-hosted-prod-usw2-blockmgr):
```
- continuous_batch_threshold: 0.65
- eviction.window_ms: 250
- block_size_hint: dynamic
+ continuous_batch_threshold: 0.5
+ eviction.window_ms: 1000
+ block_size_hint: 256KB
+ max_metadata_inflight: 30
```
We'll patch via config service so it's non-disruptive.

nate: I'll run the config patch. can someone pause autoscaler for the pool? we don't want new nodes mixing with canary.

ops-bot: autoscaler toggle accepted by @maria. Autoscaler for pool paused.

maria: rolling config patch to 2 canaries now: ``curl -XPOST https://config.internal/patch -d @patch.json``. patch id 9832.

sam: watching metrics. eviction_rate (per-min) down from 8x -> 3x within 60s of patch on canary. metadata RPC latency tail dropped 40%.

customer-success: update for acme-inc: "We've identified an internal cache eviction regression and applied a targeted mitigation. We're seeing improvements; will follow up with root cause and timeline." Do we want to add ETA?

jordan: hold ETA until we observe 15m of stable behavior. initial rollback to threshold + metadata throttle looks promising.

maria: scaling rollout to remaining 8 nodes in pool after 10m stable window. will prepare canary logs for postmortem.

nate: deployed to all nodes. eviction churn normalized to ~1.1x baseline. CPU tail latencies back under 95th target.

sam: note: we still see a handful of long-running sessions with high KV block counts which triggered blockmgr refcount warnings. I recommend adding a guarded GC pass to reconcile leaked metadata instead of brute eviction. I can run a safe reconcile job that walks leases and fixes refs.

maria: please schedule the reconcile job after 30m to avoid interfering with rollout. sam, coordinate with @ops-bot for a low-impact window.

ops-bot: reconcile job scheduled (job id rc-2026) to run at +40m. Will stream logs to this thread.

customer-success: acme-inc acknowledged our update, asking for follow-up postmortem and mitigations to prevent recurrence. They're appreciative of the quick response.

jordan: postmortem TODOs: 1) root cause analysis on why cf3a2 changed batching behaviour vs expectation 2) add unit/integration tests for block_size heuristics 3) add circuit breaker on metadata ops when rate exceeds X 4) communicate to customers with a short RCA and planned fixes.

nate: I'll open a PR to pin continuous-batch heuristics in the runtime with an explicit safety gate and add a feature-flag to allow future kernel changes to opt-in.

sam: add a monitoring alert: if eviction_rate > 3x baseline AND metadata_rpc_5xx > 50 in 5m -> page oncall. current thresholds were too permissive.

maria: quick notes on customer impact: ~0.6% of host gen requests returned 500s during the spike window; worst for long-context tenants. No data exfiltration or integrity issues observed. SLA hits under review for acme-inc.

customer-success: I updated INC-4319 with latest notes and cc'd account team. They asked for a standby contact. Putting Jordan as main follow-up.

ops-bot: reconcile job rc-2026 started. streaming logs: "reconcile: scanned 12k leases, repaired 34 refcounts, cleared 0 stuck locks"

sam: nice. after reconcile some of the refcount warnings went away. overall eviction noise now at baseline.

maria: marking incident as mitigated for now. We'll keep monitoring for 2h. Starting incident handoff prep.

jordan: creating a short customer-facing blurb for acme-inc and a more detailed RCA draft.

nate: follow-ups opened: PR#5821 (safety gate), MON-3392 (alert tuning), PMT-728 (blocksize unit tests), IR-631 (postmortem).

customer-success: acme-inc accepted the update, will wait for RCA. thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria: final notes for handoff: state = mitigated, root cause hypothesis = batching heuristic change increased long-seq grouping -> block hotness -> metadata RPC storm -> reflexive eviction; immediate mitigation = config rollback + metadata inflight throttle + reconcile job; customer impact = transient elevated 5xx for small subset (0.6%). owners: sam (runtime), nate (deploy/patch), jordan (customer comms).

incidents-bot: Incident state updated -> MITIGATED by @maria at 2123456862. Please file postmortem with timeline and attach logs.

jordan: will kick off postmortem doc and link here when ready.

maria: thanks all. leaving thread open for any late regressions.
